title: Which shapes leave gaps?
_map: Tiles with no gaps (stretch). Big idea: some shapes fit together with no gaps (tessellation). Creative: which tiles can cover the barn floor perfectly? Invent a new tile that works.
_story: Steve wants to tile the barn floor so no mud shows through. It tries squares, triangles, hexagons and circles. Circles leave gaps everywhere.
_stepChain: shapes (corners-and-sides) → cover a floor with no gaps → squares work → triangles work → hexagons work (like honeycomb) → circles leave gaps → shapes that fit with no gaps tessellate

talk.ask: Why can't circles cover a floor without gaps?
talk.goodAnswer: they're curved, so they only touch at points and leave gaps between.

handsOn: Cut out lots of the same shape from paper and try to cover a page with no gaps and no overlaps. Try squares, then circles, then a shape you invent.

narration.speaker: steve
narration.text: My barn floor is muddy! I want to cover it with tiles, with no gaps for mud to squelch through. Squares work perfectly.
Triangles work too: point up, point down, point up. No gaps!

narration.speaker: steve
narration.text: Circles are my favourite. I'll use circles!

question.prompt: Will circles cover the floor with no gaps?
question.onRight: Yes, you predicted it. Curved edges only touch at points, so gaps are left between them.

0.mistake: hasn't pictured how curved edges meet
0.hint: Imagine pushing coins together on a table. Do they fit with no spaces?
0.say: Circles only touch at tiny points. There are always little gaps between them, where the mud would show.

question.reveal: Gaps everywhere! Mud would squelch through.

narration.text: Hexagons, with 6 sides, fit perfectly too. That's why bees build honeycomb from them. When a shape covers a floor with no gaps and no overlaps, we say it tessellates.
Can you invent a new tile that tessellates? Here's a trick: start with a square, cut a bump out of one side, and stick it on the opposite side. It still fits with no gaps!

rule.text: Shapes that tessellate fit with no gaps.
rule.ask: Can you say which shapes tessellate, and why circles don't? Say it out loud. Then tap the eye.
rule.spoken: Squares, triangles and hexagons tessellate: they fit together with no gaps. Circles don't, because they're curved.

bonus.prompt: Bonus: do shapes with 5 equal sides (pentagons) tessellate?
bonus.reveal: Not regular ones! They leave gaps. But some stretched pentagons do tessellate. Mathematicians are still finding new ones.
